correctness.rationale: At known fixed μ, differentiating the busy-period Bessel density cancels its apparent 1/λ score singularity, giving S=−y+y√(μ/λ)I₂/I₁. Positive series give I₂/I₁≤z/4, hence |S|≤y+μy²/2; for λ≤μ/4 the series also give g≤μ exp(−μy/4). Dominated convergence to the exponential density and score μy²/2−y gives 2/μ². At the other endpoint, z|I₂/I₁−1| is bounded on the positive axis by the small- and large-z expansions and continuity. Thus S=(√(μ/λ)−1)Y plus a uniform bounded remainder for λ≥μ/2. With d=μ−λ the first two Laplace derivatives are E[Y]=1/d and E[Y²]=2μ/d³; the cross term and bounded remainder square are Oμ(1). The leading term is 2μ/[λ(√μ+√λ)²d], which is 1/(2μd)+Oμ(1), not just a relative equivalence. Substitution into the fixed-parameter constants proves both pairs of limits and the stated ratios, with the observation-horizon limit taken first. The derivation does not use the originating paper's incorrect Y|X argument: conditional on X=k, there are 2k−1 queue jumps, and their holding times are Exp(λ+μ), so the conditional law is Erlang(2k−1,λ+μ), not a λ-independent Erlang(k,μ). Only the marginal formulas are used. Frozen verify.py and verification notes were inspected, not executed. Fresh fixed-order scaled Gauss–Laguerre quadrature at μ=1 gave I_Y=1.99900141683 at ρ=10⁻⁴ and (1−ρ)I_Y=0.50054863 at ρ=0.99; these are finite checks only.
